pr_title: JavaClassWrapper: Improve handling of typed array arguments
pr_body:
Fixes https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/102712

There are 3 issues that come from that:

- [X] Method selection doesn't take typed arrays (including the `Packed*Array` types) into account when selected an overloaded method
- ~~[x] vararg methods aren't supported~~
- [x] Arrays of `JavaObject`s aren't supported (this one I noticed while working on this)

~~So far, this PR only fixes the first one, which is why this is currently marked as DRAFT.~~

**UPDATE:** All the issues are fixed now in my testing!

**UPDATE 2:** I ended up deciding to remove the explicit support for varargs - see [this comment](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/102817#issuecomment-2659500068).
pr_comments:
I've now got all the issues fixed in my testing!

However, this does change quite a large amount of code, and will need a thorough review.

> The changes are small and scoped enough they should be safe to include in 4.4.

The ship _may_ have sailed on Godot 4.4, but it'd fine for this to end up in 4.4.1.

In my latest push, I added one of the same efficiency improvements as I did in PR https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/103375, where JNI fills some the arrays (the ones where the types match) rather than us going element by element. I have a test project that comprehensively tests all the conversion branches in this one, so I'm pretty confident about this update!

issue_context.title: When using JavaClassWrapper, calling a method with multiple overloaded parameters will cause an error.
comments:
Thanks!

I'll spend some more time digging into this later after putting together a project to test, but looking at this specific example, it seems like this might be the expected behavior:

1. In GDScript, `["abc"]` is an untyped `Array`, so I would expect it to match any array type on the Java side, and just attempt to convert all its elements to the Java type (which in this case I think would turn `"abc"` to `0`). I don't know if this actually works (I'll do some testing later), but this would at least need to be a typed `Array[String]` in GDScript, in order to not match with `IntArray` in Kotlin
2. Calling a vararg function in GDScript is not equivalent to passing an array. So, I would expect something like `javaClass.testMethod(1, "abc", "123")` to match the vararg one, but not the example given above (`javaClass.testMethod(1,["asd"])`). But I suspect that `JavaClassWrapper` doesn't support vararg methods at all at the moment - another thing I'll look into later :-)

That's not to say that even if this is the expected behavior for this example, that there aren't bugs here - but we may need to use a different example as a reference.

I finally set up a test project and can confirm that there are some bugs here, namely:

-  Method selection doesn't take typed arrays (including the `Packed*Array` types) into account when selected an overloaded method
-  vararg methods aren't supported
- Arrays of `JavaObject`s aren't supported (this one I noticed while working on this)

I've started PR https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/102817, which, so far, addresses only the first one.

I'm sure we can fix them all, however, I'm not sure we'll manage it before Godot 4.4-stable's release - this may end up being something cherry-picked for 4.4.1.

> 我终于搭建了一个测试项目，可以确认这里存在一些 bug，即：
> 
> * 选择重载方法时，方法选择不考虑类型化数组（包括类型）`Packed*Array`
> * 不支持 vararg 方法
> * 不支持 s 数组（我在处理此内容时注意到这一点）`JavaObject`
> 
> 我已经开始了 PR [#102817](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/102817)，到目前为止，它只解决了第一个问题。
> 
> 我确信我们可以修复它们，但是，我不确定我们能否在 Godot 4.4-stable 发布之前管理它 - 这最终可能会成为 4.4.1 的精选内容。

I’m really looking forward to the further development of this feature!
Keeping the issue open as the pull request that fixes this hasn't been merged yet.

review_comments: We should check that `c` is valid before proceeding.

We would have checked this earlier on line 224.

This process goes in two phase: a validation phase, where it reports errors about any of the provided arguments, and then a calling phase where (if there were no validation errors) it marshals the data into the Java types and actually calls the method. This would have gotten caught in the validation phase.

However, it's no problem to add `if (c) { ... }`, so I have done that in my latest push :-)
Does the copy logic not work for `short`?

Not with the way that I decided to convert from `PackedInt32Array`: it's set up to treat each item in the `PackedInt32Array` as representing a single `short`.

If we decided that each item in the `PackedInt32Array` represented 2 `short`s (with one of them shifted two bytes to the left) then we could copy directly. However, that didn't seem like the most friendly for developers - my guess is that they would assume it was the former.

Although, that was just a judgement call I made! If anyone thinks otherwise, let's discuss :-)

Actually, thinking about this a little more, I don't think we actually could treat each item in `PackedInt32Array` as representing two `short`s: how would you pass an array with an odd number of items? There'd be no way to indicate that the last element didn't exist.

I think the way I'm doing the conversion is really the only way to do it if we use `PackedInt32Array`. If we wanted to pack them tighter, we could use `PackedByteArray`, but that would be so tricky to use from GDScript.

I'm happy with the judgement call I made here: it optimizes for ease of use by the developer, not performance or lower memory usage. I don't think APIs that take `short[]` are super common anyway, so odds are this conversion won't get used that much
Yeah, I don't really remember the last time I used short[].
